rulingTitle: Reported repo gate B1 fails this required confined-run contract: the ordinary zero-exit spawn case times out, causing the runner to return 1. Confined runtime hygiene is not yet reliably green.

action.reason: The branch fix (f96e1eeda) targets the likely causes: it skips the ps case when ps answers nothing, gives the confined run the 60s runner budget, and adds a beforeAll that absorbs the first-launch cost. No assertion was weakened and no ordinary spawn case was skipped. I could not run a working sandbox here. The CI test:confined step is the enforcing gate and fails the job on any non-zero exit, so a residual flake would show up there.

rationale: The finding asks for a demonstration on a working sandbox that this review cannot perform. The cause was addressed in code and CI enforces the result. Confirm the first CI run of test:confined.

rulingTitle: Heartbeats depend on polling completing. The config accepts ciPollMs above 60 seconds; a virtual-clock reproduction with pollMs=300000 logs its first heartbeat after five minutes, violating the promised 60-second bound. Slow forge calls can likewise suppress progress.

action.reason: Fixed in f96e1eeda. The heartbeat runs on its own unref'd scheduled interval, cancelled on every return path. The wait between polls is sliced to fit within CI_WAIT_HEARTBEAT_MS and the slices sum to pollMs, so the polling cadence is unchanged. The commit adds long-poll and slow-poll test cases that reproduce the finding.

rationale: The finding describes behaviour from before the fix. I read the current ci-wait.ts and it meets the 60-second bound and AC-13.
